name: Job Seeker Visa (Visado de Búsqueda de Empleo)

requirements.blocker_text: This preferential category is exempt from the labour-market test and is available to children and grandchildren of Spaniards by origin.
This requires a qualified profile matching, by analogy, the SEPE Catálogo de Ocupaciones de Difícil Cobertura (shortage occupations catalogue).

evidence_required.document: Proof of Spanish ancestry (child/grandchild of Spaniard by origin), or documented qualification matching a shortage occupation

sources.title: BOE — Real Decreto 1155/2024 (Reglamento de Extranjería), Arts. 43-45, job-seeker visa provisions

notes: Duration quadrupled under the 2025 reform — 12 months, up from just 3 months under the prior reglamento, a genuine and significant improvement worth flagging clearly since the OLD 3-month figure likely still circulates on unrefreshed tier-3 pages. Does NOT authorize work during the search itself (work_rights: none) — the holder must find a job offer, at which point the EMPLOYER files a separate cuenta ajena work authorization; this two-step structure is similar to Germany's Job Seeker permit but with the notable difference that Germany's version does allow limited work during the search while Spain's does not. Preferential exemption for children/grandchildren of Spaniards by origin is Spain's closest analogue to an ancestry-based route in this dataset, though it manifests here as a job-seeker exemption rather than a standalone immigration status — this is part of why Spain has no dedicated 'ancestry' category route the way Portugal and the UK do (see es_naturalisation notes for the fuller picture on Spain's ancestry-adjacent provisions). Continuity of residence matters for anyone using this route: an absence exceeding 6 months would break the continuity needed for eventual permanent residence/nationality timelines, even though the job-seeker period itself isn't calculated toward those clocks.
